label: Choice-cell determination: invariant levels explain only the range; selection is contingent
paraphrase: Analyst formulation on any local STIT frame with an outcome map, where each agent is one explanatory level of a source and explaining 'the actual outcome rather than y' is Cstit of 'outcome is not y' (the actual cell excludes y): a cell-level analogue of SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_2 (ContrastRelevant, disambiguation 59b60fe6), not one of its senses and not bridged to it. (1) A level explains the contrast exactly when y is outside its actual cell range. (2) For any candidate set T0 containing the realized range, T0 minus the cell range is the disjoint union of T0 minus the realized range and the realized range minus the cell range (the #1953 decomposition). (3) A level with a single cell explains a contrast exactly when y is not realized by any history of the scope. (4) Such a level selects the actual outcome exactly when the outcome is not contingent in the scope. (5) Selection holds exactly when every rival outcome is excluded. (6) A level that selects a contingent actual outcome deliberatively sees to its own actual cell (Dstit), and no single-cell level sees to that cell. (7) Two levels with the same actual cell explain the same contrasts (definitional: Cstit reads only cells). (8) A level whose actual cell is the actual outcome class selects, and with a contingent outcome sees to its own cell: the outcome partition itself meets the standard, so determination on cells cannot tell explaining the selection from re-describing it. Nothing about rationality, chance or goodness is typed.
